author: Al Jazeera English
description:
US President Donald Trump has signed two executive orders seeking to limit birthright citizenship in the United States as part of his broader immigration crackdown. The measures expand the categories of people whose children could be denied automatic US citizenship, while also targeting so-called "birth tourism" by directing the secretaries of state and homeland security to tighten procedures against travellers seeking to give birth in the US. The new restrictions also cover children born to people classified as "alien enemies" or members of designated terrorist groups. The measures are far narrower than Trump's January 2025 attempt to end birthright citizenship, which the Supreme Court rejected in June, citing more than 160 years of legal precedent. Trump called the ruling "very unfair," saying birthright citizenship had become "a joke" and that his administration was "ending it a different way." The executive orders are expected to face fresh legal challenges. 

Al Jazeera’s Rosilan
title: Trump signs new executive orders to limit birthright citizenship

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Iran says it has reached an understanding with Oman on the geographical coordinates of a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, bringing weeks of negotiations closer to a formal agreement.
Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi says almost all issues remain under discussion, including the route map, transit arrangements, and the movement of vessels entering and leaving the waterway.
Tehran says bilateral agreements with Oman are close to being finalised and insists the talks are taking place without outside interference.
Iranian officials argue any agreement would not restore conditions before the conflict, blaming US military actions and a naval blockade for disrupting navigation.
Washington rejects reports that Iran would control traffic through the strait, saying any temporary route should not require permits, approvals or fees.

title: Iran says Hormuz shipping route framework with Oman is nearly complete

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
US President Donald Trump says ongoing talks between Washington and Tehran could avert a new US military strike on Iran.
Speaking at a public event in Las Vegas, Trump claimed the United States had been prepared to launch what he described as its biggest military attacks since World War Two before Iran sought talks.
He alleged Iranian officials had asked Washington not to carry out the strikes, although Tehran has denied making such a request.
Trump said negotiations are continuing and insisted Iran now "respects" the United States.
He also repeated that no previous US president had taken such a firm approach towards Iran, while maintaining that Tehran must never be allowed to acquire a nuclear weapon.
